questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Nobel Prize is awarded annually in how many categories?
questions.explanation: The Nobel Prize is awarded in 6 categories: Physics, Chemistry, Physiology/Medicine, Literature, Peace, and Economic Sciences. 4 is wrong — it excludes Peace and Economics; 5 is wrong — it excludes the Economics prize (added in 1969); 7 is wrong — there is no seventh category.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Bharat Ratna:

(i) It is the highest civilian award of India.
(ii) It was instituted in 1954.
(iii) A maximum of five awards can be given in a year.
(iv) It can be awarded posthumously.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian honour (i-correct), was instituted in 1954 (ii-correct), and can be awarded posthumously (iv-correct). Statement (iii) is wrong — there is a maximum of three Bharat Ratna awards in a year, not five.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Pulitzer Prize is primarily associated with excellence in:
options: Journalism and literary achievements in the USA
questions.correctAnswer: Journalism and literary achievements in the USA
questions.explanation: The Pulitzer Prize honours achievements in newspaper, magazine, and online journalism, literature, and musical composition in the United States. Scientific research is wrong — that is recognized by Nobel and other science prizes; international peace is wrong — that is the Nobel Peace Prize; sports is wrong — the Pulitzer does not cover athletics.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Rabindranath Tagore was the first Asian to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.
Reason (R): He was awarded the Nobel Prize in 1913 for his collection of poems 'Gitanjali'.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Tagore was indeed the first Asian Nobel Laureate in Literature (A is correct). He received it in 1913 for Gitanjali (R is correct and directly explains why he holds this distinction). Option 2 is wrong because R provides the specific facts supporting A; Option 3 is wrong because R is factually accurate; Option 4 is wrong because A is also correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are recipients of the Bharat Ratna?

(i) Sachin Tendulkar
(ii) APJ Abdul Kalam
(iii) Amitabh Bachchan
(iv) C.V. Raman

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Sachin Tendulkar (2014), APJ Abdul Kalam (1997), and C.V. Raman (1954) are all Bharat Ratna recipients (i, ii, iv correct). Amitabh Bachchan (iii) is wrong — he has received the Padma Shri (1984) and Padma Vibhushan (2015) but not the Bharat Ratna.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award (now renamed Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award) is India's highest honour for achievement in:
questions.explanation: The Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award (formerly Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna) is India's highest sporting honour given to outstanding sportspersons. Literature/arts is wrong — Sahitya Akademi and Padma awards cover that; scientific discovery is wrong — that is honoured by Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize; social service is wrong — Padma awards cover that.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following awards with the fields they honour:

Column I:
(a) Nobel Prize in Physics
(b) Booker Prize
(c) Grammy Award
(d) Arjuna Award

Column II:
(i) Music
(ii) Sports
(iii) Literature (fiction)
(iv) Physics

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Nobel Prize in Physics honours physics (a-iv); Booker Prize honours fiction writing (b-iii); Grammy Awards honour music (c-i); Arjuna Award honours sports achievement (d-ii). Option 2 swaps physics and literature; Option 3 swaps literature and music; Option 4 swaps music and sports.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Padma Awards:

(i) Padma Vibhushan is the second highest civilian award after Bharat Ratna.
(ii) Padma Bhushan is the third highest civilian award.
(iii) Padma Shri is the fourth highest civilian award.
(iv) Padma Awards are announced on Independence Day (15 August).

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Padma Vibhushan is the 2nd highest (i-correct), Padma Bhushan the 3rd (ii-correct), and Padma Shri the 4th highest civilian award (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because Padma Awards are announced on Republic Day eve (25 January), not Independence Day.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Dronacharya Award is given to outstanding:
questions.explanation: The Dronacharya Award recognizes excellence in sports coaching and mentoring, named after the legendary teacher Dronacharya from the Mahabharata. Sportspersons for lifetime is wrong — that is the Dhyan Chand Award; sports journalists is wrong — no such specific national award exists; sports administrators is wrong — the Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puraskar covers that.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize is one of the most prestigious science awards in India.
Reason (R): It is awarded by the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) to scientists below the age of 45 for outstanding contributions.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: The Bhatnagar Prize is India's top science award (A is correct). CSIR awards it to scientists under 45 for outstanding work (R is correct and explains its prestige — its selectivity and CSIR backing make it prestigious). Option 2 is wrong because R explains why it is prestigious; Option 3 is wrong because R is factually correct; Option 4 is wrong because A is also correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Magsaysay Award, often called the 'Nobel Prize of Asia', is given by which country?
questions.explanation: The Ramon Magsaysay Award is given by the Ramon Magsaysay Award Foundation based in Manila, Philippines, named after a former Philippine president. Japan is wrong — Japan gives the Kyoto Prize; India is wrong — India gives its own national awards; South Korea is wrong — it has no connection to this award.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correct about the Nobel Prize?

(i) It was established by the will of Alfred Nobel, a Swedish inventor.
(ii) The first Nobel Prizes were awarded in 1901.
(iii) The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo, Norway.
(iv) All Nobel Prizes are awarded in Stockholm, Sweden.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Alfred Nobel's will established the prizes (i-correct), first awarded in 1901 (ii-correct), and the Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo, Norway (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because not ALL prizes are given in Stockholm — the Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo, Norway, while the other five are given in Stockholm.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The __________ Award is India's highest literary honour, given annually by the Sahitya Akademi for outstanding literary work in Indian languages.
questions.explanation: The Jnanpith Award is India's highest literary honour (though the Sahitya Akademi also gives awards, the Jnanpith is considered the highest). Sahitya Akademi Award is wrong — it is given by Sahitya Akademi but is a different, lower-tier award; Saraswati Samman is wrong — it is given by the K.K. Birla Foundation; Vyas Samman is wrong — it is also given by K.K. Birla Foundation for Hindi literature.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following Indian national awards with their fields:

Column I:
(a) Arjuna Award
(b) Sahitya Akademi Award
(c) Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize
(d) Dadasaheb Phalke Award

Column II:
(i) Cinema
(ii) Science
(iii) Literature
(iv) Sports

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Arjuna Award is for sports (a-iv); Sahitya Akademi Award for literature (b-iii); Bhatnagar Prize for science (c-ii); Dadasaheb Phalke Award for cinema (d-i). Option 2 swaps literature and science; Option 3 assigns literature to Arjuna; Option 4 swaps cinema and science.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: C.V. Raman won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930 for his work on:
questions.explanation: Sir C.V. Raman was awarded the Nobel Prize for his discovery of the Raman Effect — the scattering of light when it passes through a transparent medium. Theory of relativity is wrong — that was Einstein; discovery of neutron is wrong — that was Chadwick; photoelectric effect is wrong — Einstein won for that in 1921.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Arjuna Award:

(i) It is given for consistent outstanding performance in sports over four years.
(ii) It was instituted in 1961.
(iii) It carries a cash prize, a bronze statuette, and a scroll.
(iv) It is the highest sports honour in India.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Arjuna Award requires consistent performance over 4 years (i-correct), was instituted in 1961 (ii-correct), and includes cash, statuette, and scroll (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award (formerly Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna) is India's highest sports honour, not the Arjuna Award.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Fields Medal is the highest honour in which academic discipline?
questions.explanation: The Fields Medal is the most prestigious award in mathematics, given every four years to mathematicians under 40. Physics is wrong — that has the Nobel Prize; Chemistry is wrong — also has a Nobel Prize; Economics is wrong — that has the Nobel Memorial Prize and the Abel Prize is also for mathematics.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Mother Teresa received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979.
Reason (R): She was honoured for her decades of humanitarian work among the poorest of the poor in Kolkata, India.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Mother Teresa received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979 (A is correct). Her humanitarian work with the destitute in Kolkata was the basis for the award (R is correct and explains A). Option 2 is wrong because R directly explains why she received it; Option 3 is wrong because R is factually accurate; Option 4 is wrong because A is also correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows Nobel Prize winners from India:

| Laureate | Year | Category |
|----------|------|----------|
| C.V. Raman | 1930 | Physics |
| Har Gobind Khorana | 1968 | Medicine |
| Mother Teresa | 1979 | Peace |
| Amartya Sen | 1998 | Economics |
| Kailash Satyarthi | 2014 | Peace |

How many years elapsed between India's first and last Nobel Prize listed above?
questions.explanation: First: C.V. Raman in 1930. Last listed: Kailash Satyarthi in 2014. Gap = 2014 − 1930 = 84 years. 74 years is wrong (uses 2004 instead of 2014); 64 years is wrong (uses 1994); 94 years is wrong (uses 2024).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Oscar Award (Academy Award) is associated with excellence in:
questions.explanation: The Academy Awards (Oscars) honour excellence in cinema and the film industry. Television is wrong — that is the Emmy Awards; music recording is wrong — that is the Grammy Awards; theatrical performances is wrong — that is the Tony Awards.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following Indians have won the Nobel Prize in Economics?

(i) Amartya Sen
(ii) Abhijit Banerjee
(iii) Raghuram Rajan
(iv) Manmohan Singh

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Amartya Sen (1998) and Abhijit Banerjee (2019) are Nobel laureates in Economics (i, ii correct). Raghuram Rajan (iii) is wrong — he is a noted economist and former RBI Governor but has not won the Nobel Prize; Manmohan Singh (iv) is wrong — he is an economist and former PM but not a Nobel laureate.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Gallantry Award 'Param Vir Chakra' is India's highest military decoration for:
options: Distinguished service of the highest order
Conspicuous bravery or self-sacrifice in the presence of the enemy
questions.correctAnswer: Conspicuous bravery or self-sacrifice in the presence of the enemy
questions.explanation: Param Vir Chakra (PVC) is awarded for the most conspicuous bravery or self-sacrifice in the face of the enemy. Distinguished service is wrong — that is covered by Padma awards; military strategy is wrong — no such specific award; long service is wrong — that is the Long Service and Good Conduct Medal.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Dadasaheb Phalke Award:

(i) It is India's highest award in cinema.
(ii) It is named after Dhundiraj Govind Phalke, the father of Indian cinema.
(iii) It was instituted in 1969.
(iv) It is given annually by the National Film Development Corporation.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Dadasaheb Phalke Award is India's highest cinema honour (i-correct), named after the father of Indian cinema (ii-correct), and instituted in 1969 (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because it is given by the Directorate of Film Festivals (under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting), not by NFDC.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following Nobel Prize categories with their awarding institutions:

Column I:
(a) Nobel Peace Prize
(b) Nobel Prize in Literature
(c) Nobel Prize in Chemistry
(d) Nobel Prize in Economics

Column II:
(i) Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences
(ii) Norwegian Nobel Committee
(iii) Swedish Academy
(iv) Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Peace Prize is awarded by the Norwegian Nobel Committee (a-ii); Literature by the Swedish Academy (b-iii); Chemistry by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences (c-i); Economics also by the Royal Swedish Academy (d-iv). Option 2 swaps Peace and Literature; Option 3 swaps Literature and Chemistry institutions; Option 4 swaps Chemistry and Economics.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the number of Nobel Prizes won by selected countries (cumulative, approximate):

| Country | Total Nobel Prizes |
|---------|-------------------|
| USA | 400 |
| UK | 135 |
| Germany | 110 |
| France | 70 |
| India | 10 |

What is the approximate ratio of US Nobel Prizes to India's Nobel Prizes?
questions.explanation: USA has 400 and India has 10. Ratio = 400:10 = 40:1. 20:1 is wrong (would require India to have 20); 30:1 is wrong (would require India to have about 13); 50:1 is wrong (would require India to have 8).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Sahitya Akademi Award is given for outstanding literary works in how many Indian languages?
questions.explanation: The Sahitya Akademi recognizes literary works in 24 languages — 22 Scheduled Languages plus English and Rajasthani. 18 is wrong — it's fewer than the actual count; 22 is wrong — it counts only scheduled languages without English and Rajasthani; 26 is wrong — it exceeds the current count.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following statements about the Abel Prize are correct?

(i) It is awarded annually for outstanding contributions to mathematics.
(ii) It is given by the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters.
(iii) It was first awarded in 2003.
(iv) It is named after Indian mathematician Srinivasa Ramanujan.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: The Abel Prize is for mathematics (i-correct), given by the Norwegian Academy (ii-correct), and first awarded in 2003 (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because it is named after Norwegian mathematician Niels Henrik Abel, not Srinivasa Ramanujan.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Kailash Satyarthi, who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014, is known for his work in:
options: Children's rights and ending child labour
questions.correctAnswer: Children's rights and ending child labour
questions.explanation: Kailash Satyarthi won the Nobel Peace Prize for his struggle against child labour and advocacy for children's rights. Environmental conservation is wrong — that is associated with Wangari Maathai; nuclear disarmament is wrong — that relates to ICAN; women's education is wrong — that is associated with Malala Yousafzai (co-winner with Satyarthi).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Booker Prize:

(i) It is awarded for the best novel written in English.
(ii) It was previously open only to Commonwealth citizens but is now open to all English-language novels.
(iii) Arundhati Roy won it in 1997 for 'The God of Small Things'.
(iv) It is awarded by the Government of United Kingdom.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Booker Prize is for the best English novel (i-correct), was expanded in 2014 to all English-language works (ii-correct), and Arundhati Roy won in 1997 (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because it is sponsored by private organizations (previously Booker McConnell, now Crankstart Foundation), not the UK government.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Gallantry Awards of India in descending order of precedence are:
options: Maha Vir Chakra, Param Vir Chakra, Vir Chakra
Vir Chakra, Param Vir Chakra, Maha Vir Chakra
Param Vir Chakra, Vir Chakra, Maha Vir Chakra
Param Vir Chakra, Maha Vir Chakra, Vir Chakra
questions.correctAnswer: Param Vir Chakra, Maha Vir Chakra, Vir Chakra
questions.explanation: The correct descending order is: Param Vir Chakra (highest), Maha Vir Chakra (second), Vir Chakra (third). Option 2 incorrectly places Maha Vir Chakra first; Option 3 incorrectly places Vir Chakra first; Option 4 incorrectly swaps Maha Vir Chakra and Vir Chakra.
